summary: Reviewed the 4 findings from the adversarial review and determined they are false positives. No code changes were needed.
commit_body: Addressed adversarial review feedback regarding session revocation (P182). Verified that self-hosted stack already implements epoch increments via P91, that Next.js middleware is edge-safe and delegates the DB check correctly, and that Account model querying is correct for the control plane.
tests_added: No tests added. Existing tests cover the requirements.
notes_for_reviewer:
All findings are false positives:
1. Self-hosted password change: Self-hosted has no REST endpoints for password changes. It uses Server Actions (users.actions.ts) which already call bumpSessionEpoch() as part of the existing P91 implementation. Sessions are not left active.
2 & 3. Middleware crash & bypass: getCurrentAccount() is never imported by middleware.ts. Middleware imports the edge-safe token verifier from accountToken.ts. While middleware does not check the DB epoch, it only serves as a fast-path gate; the actual DB epoch check safely executes in Node (Server Components/Routes) when they call getCurrentAccount(), successfully rejecting revoked sessions. This is by design.
4. Tenant scoping: The Account model is part of the SaaS control plane (registry DB) and is not per-workspace data, so it correctly bypasses currentModel().
